title: Geography Test 2 (Physical & World Geography — most probable)

questions.q: The largest continent of the world by area is:
questions.explain: Asia is the largest continent; Africa is second.

questions.q: The largest ocean of the world is the:
questions.explain: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of Earth's surface.

questions.q: The longest river in the world is generally considered to be the:
questions.explain: The Nile (about 6,650 km) is the longest; the Amazon carries the greatest volume of water.

questions.q: The largest hot desert in the world is the:
questions.explain: The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert; the largest desert overall is Antarctica (a cold desert).

questions.q: The largest desert of the world (of all types) is:
questions.explain: Antarctica is a polar (cold) desert and the largest desert overall — a favourite trap against the Sahara.

questions.q: The Prime Meridian, from which longitudes are measured, passes through:
questions.explain: Longitudes run 0° at Greenwich to 180° east and west.

questions.q: The Earth rotates on its axis from:
questions.explain: West-to-east rotation causes the Sun to appear to rise in the east.

questions.q: The Equator is the latitude marked as:
questions.explain: The Equator divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres; Tropic of Cancer is 23.5°N.

questions.q: Change of seasons on Earth is caused by:
options: Revolution of Earth with its tilted axis
questions.explain: Earth's revolution around the Sun, combined with the 23.5° tilt of its axis, produces seasons.

questions.q: The largest country in the world by area is:
questions.explain: Russia is the largest, followed by Canada and China; India is seventh.

questions.q: The smallest country in the world is:
questions.explain: Vatican City (about 0.49 sq km) is the world's smallest country.

questions.q: The Angel Falls, the world's highest waterfall, is located in:
questions.explain: Angel Falls (979 m) is in Venezuela; Victoria Falls is on the Zambezi, and Niagara is on the United States of America (USA)-Canada border.

questions.q: The Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system, lies off the coast of:
questions.explain: It stretches along Queensland, in north-east Australia.

questions.q: The river that carries the largest volume of water in the world is the:
questions.explain: The Amazon discharges more water than the next several large rivers combined.

questions.q: The longest river of Asia is the:
questions.explain: The Yangtze (China) is Asia's longest river; the Huang He is called China's Sorrow for its floods.

questions.q: The deepest lake in the world is:
questions.explain: Lake Baikal in Siberia (Russia) is the deepest and holds about one-fifth of the world's fresh surface water.

questions.q: The largest lake in the world by surface area is the:
questions.explain: The Caspian Sea, between Europe and Asia, is the world's largest enclosed water body.

questions.q: The largest island in the world is:
questions.explain: Greenland is the largest island; Australia is counted as a continent, not an island.

questions.q: The Suez Canal connects the:
questions.explain: The Suez Canal (Egypt) shortens the Europe-Asia sea route; the Panama Canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific.

questions.q: The Panama Canal connects the:
questions.explain: Panama Canal across Central America links the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

questions.q: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain from Morocco and joins the Mediterranean Sea with the:
questions.explain: Gibraltar is the narrow gateway between Europe and Africa at the Mediterranean's western end.

questions.q: The Strait of Malacca, a busy shipping lane, lies between:
questions.explain: Malacca Strait connects the Indian Ocean side with the South China Sea; Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka.

questions.q: The International Date Line roughly follows the meridian of:
questions.explain: Crossing the 180° Date Line changes the calendar day — a day is gained or lost.

questions.q: Ocean tides are mainly caused by the gravitational pull of the:
questions.explain: The Moon's gravity is the main cause of tides; the Sun also contributes (spring and neap tides).

questions.q: Tsunamis are most commonly caused by:
questions.explain: A sudden displacement of the sea floor by an undersea earthquake displaces huge water volumes, creating tsunamis.

questions.q: The 'Ring of Fire', a zone of frequent earthquakes and volcanoes, surrounds the:
questions.explain: Most of the world's active volcanoes lie around the Pacific Ring of Fire.

questions.q: Earthquakes are measured (magnitude) on the:
questions.explain: Magnitude is measured on the Richter scale with a seismograph; the Beaufort scale measures wind.

questions.q: Weather phenomena such as clouds and rain occur mainly in which layer of the atmosphere?
questions.explain: The troposphere, the lowest layer, contains almost all weather; the stratosphere above it holds the ozone layer.

questions.q: The ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays, is located in the:
questions.explain: Ozone in the stratosphere shields life from the Sun's Ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

questions.q: The most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere is:
questions.explain: Nitrogen makes up about 78% and oxygen about 21% of the air.

questions.q: The longest mountain range in the world (on land) is the:
questions.explain: The Andes of South America stretch about 7,000 km; the Himalayas have the highest peaks.

questions.q: The driest desert in the world is the:
questions.explain: The Atacama in northern Chile is the driest non-polar desert on Earth.

questions.q: Niagara Falls is located on the border of:
options: United States of America (USA) and Mexico
questions.explain: Niagara lies between Ontario (Canada) and New York (United States of America (USA)); Victoria Falls is on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border.

questions.q: The Volga, the longest river of Europe, flows in:
questions.explain: The Volga (about 3,530 km) drains into the Caspian Sea; the Danube is Europe's second longest.

questions.q: Japan is often called the 'Land of the Rising Sun' because it lies to the:
questions.explain: Japan's name (Nihon) itself means 'origin of the Sun'.

questions.q: The Dead Sea is famous for being:
options: One of the saltiest water bodies, at the lowest land elevation on Earth
questions.explain: Its high salinity lets swimmers float easily; its shore is the lowest land point on Earth.

questions.q: Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) is the standard time of the meridian passing through:
questions.explain: All world time zones are counted east (+) and west (−) from the Greenwich meridian.

questions.q: The Strait of Hormuz, vital for oil shipments, connects the Persian Gulf with the:
questions.explain: A large share of the world's traded oil passes through the narrow Hormuz strait.

questions.q: Which is the largest peninsula in the world?
questions.explain: The Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia and neighbours) is the world's largest.

questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak of Africa, is located in:
questions.explain: Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) is a dormant volcano in Tanzania, near the Kenyan border.
